sentences.text:
The gravamen of indictment against the applicant is that the a  SSP 1/6  ba 1585 of 2023.d had induced the first informant to enter into transactions by making a representation that Flat Nos.1503 and 2103 at Neha Residency, Abhudaya Nagar, Parel, Mumbai,
which were then being developed by the applicant, would be sold to the applicant for consideration of Rs.5 Crores each.
The first informant paid a total consideration of Rs.6,36,77,000/- towards Flat No.1503.
Transaction in respect of Flat No.1503 was completed as the applicant delivered possession of the said flat to the first informant.

However, despite receipt of the entire consideration of Rs.5 Crores in respect of Flat No.2103, the applicant did not deliver possession thereof, and, instead, handed over the same to the accused No.2 - Raman Jaybhave and thereby deceived the first informant.
4. Secondly, the applicant induced the first informant to enter into transaction to purchase Flat No.2102 at Neha Galaxy and part with an amount of Rs.1,09,00,000/-.
The applicant did not complete the said transaction and despite the cancellation of the said transaction, dishonestly retained an amount of Rs.1,09,00,000/-.

In order to defraud the first informant, the applicant allegedly got a false and fabricated MOU purported to have been executed and notarized by the mother of the first informant in the year 2020, when the mother of the first informant had passed away on 20 August 2018.
5. Learned Counsel for the Applicant submitted that the applicant submitted that the applicant had no intention to deceive the first informant.
Possession SSP 2/6  ba 1 of Flat No.1503 at Neha Residency was already delivered to the first informant.

The applicant is willing to deliver possession of Flat No.2103 in accordance with the terms Shishir Mangesh Shivapurkar vs State Of Maharashtra on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10981044/
2 of the contract between the parties.

sentences.text: It was further submitted that the allegation that the applicant had forged the MOU is wholly unfounded as the MOU was executed and notarized in the year 2017 itself, as on the basis of the photostat copies of the said MOU, such allegation of forgery is made.
Attention of the Court was invited to the copy of the MOU (page 124 of the application).
6. The applicant has filed an affidavit cum undertaking to show his bonafide.

Paragraphs 2 to 4 of the affidavit cum undertaking read as under :
 "2. I state that the primary issue giving rise to the present case is   handing over the possession of Flat No.2103 at Neha Residency located at  Sriram Tekadi Road, Ram Krishna Nagar, Parel Mumbai - 400 015 to the  first informant (hereinafter referred to as the said Flat No.2103 for short).
 3. I state that, I am ready and willing to handover the possession of  the said Flat No.2103 to the first informant subject to :
 i. The first informant depositing the outstanding amount towards  required statutory GST with applicable interest and penalties thereof, and  other dues pertaining to the registered agreement for the said Flat No.2103  at Neha Residency.

ii. The first informant depositing the outstanding amount  towards required statutory GST with applicable interest and penalties  thereof, and other dues pertaining to the registered agreement for the said  Flat No.1503 at Neha Residency.
The possession of Flat No.1503 has been  given to the first informant as of July 2019 (registered as on 20.09.2017).

4. I am ready and willing to comply with my statement of handing  over the possession to the first informant within a period of two weeks from SSP 3/6  ba 15  the date of the first informant depositing the said amounts towards required  statutory dues as per GST along with applicable penalties and interest  thereof, and other dues applicable as per points 3(i) and 3(ii) stated above.
7. Learned APP resisted the application for bail.

Mr. Merchant, learned Counsel for the first informant, submitted that the first informant is willing to accept possession of Flat No.2103 proposed to be delivered by the applicant with a view to give a quietus to the dispute.

Incontrovertibly, possession of Flat No.1503 has been delivered post execution of the instrument.
The applicant undertakes to deliver possession of Flat No.2103 as well.
Prima facie, the allegations of making forged document and forgery appear to be a matter for adjudication at the trial.
9. The applicant is in custody since 25 November 2022.

Since the applicant has also undertaken to deliver possession of Flat No.2103 and complete the transaction, undertaking contained in the affidavit can be accepted as an undertaking to the court.

10. A further statement was made by Mr. Mundargi that, as per his instructions, after release the applicant would have a meeting with the first informant to resolve the issue of appropriation of the amount of Rs.1,09,00,000 towards GST and other amount payable by the first informant in respect of Flat No.2103.
11.
The said statement is accepted.
However, it must be clarified that the Court may not be construed to have imposed any condition on the applicant for release on bail.
12. In the circumstances, the applicant deserves the exercise of discretion.

sentences.text: 4  (i) The Application stands allowed.

(ii) The Applicant - Shishir Mangesh Shivapurkar be released on bail in C.R.No.561 of 2022 registered with Kalachowki Police Station, on furnishing a PR bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- and one or two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.

(iii) The applicant shall mark his presence before Kalachowki police station on first Monday of every trimester in between 11 am to 1 pm commencing from the ba 1585 of 2023.doc next month of the release of the applicant on bail, for a period of two years or till the conclusion of the trial whichever is earlier.
(iv) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence.

The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing the facts to Court or any police officer.
(v) On being released on bail, the applicant shall furnish his contact number and residential address to the investigating officer and shall keep him updated, in case there is any change.
(vi) The applicant shall regularly attend the proceedings before the jurisdictional Court.
(vii) The undertakings in the affidavit cum undertaking dated 10 January 2024 are accepted.
(viii) Interim Application also stands disposed.

(viii) By way of abundant caution, it is clarified that the observations made hereinabove are confined for the purpose of determination of the entitlement for bail and they may not be construed as an expression of opinion on the guilt or otherwise of the applicant and the trial Court shall not be influenced by any of the observations made hereinabove.
